commentary:
Energy is the story again this morning. Brent is holding above $102 and WTI is up 1.4% near $97.4 after crude pierced $100 with the strongest term structure on record — WTI's Dec-Dec spread hit an all-time high and Brent's equivalent the firmest since the late 1990s — a screaming signal of physical tightness, reinforced by an API crude draw and reports the Houthis are closing in on a stranglehold over the Bab al-Mandeb Strait. TTF gained almost 2% and diesel is at record highs at the pump, which is precisely the problem: the energy shock is landing in the same week as US CPI and an ECB meeting where another hike looks all but certain, with the debate now about the terminal rate.

That inflation transmission is hammering rates. Treasury futures fell along the curve with the long bond off 0.3%, ten-year yields at near three-year highs after the Treasury's upsized $6bn buyback underwhelmed, and Fed officials signalling they're prepared to hike again if inflation doesn't improve. Bunds and Buxl slipped ahead of the ECB, and the BoJ adds a global channel: with 10-year JGBs around 3% — now beating hedged Treasuries for Japanese investors — a hike is expected this month, threatening a key source of foreign demand for US paper just as competition for capital intensifies.

Higher real rates and slower-growth fears crushed metals — copper down 3.6%, silver and platinum off nearly 3%, gold and iron ore lower — while equity futures are merely stabilising after Wednesday's 400-point Dow drop. In softs, coffee slumped as Colombia tariff threats were withdrawn, while sugar and cotton firmed.
